wand_of_cure_minor_wounds.name: wand of cure minor wounds
wand_of_cure_minor_wounds.lore: The Samaritan who found a stranger beaten on the Jericho road tended him with what was in his saddlebag, oil to soothe and wine to cleanse. Hedge-healers bind that mercy of the roadside into a pale stick, which closes cuts and draws the ache from bruises, though it can do little more.

wand_of_cure_light_wounds.name: wand of cure light wounds
wand_of_cure_light_wounds.lore: In Jerusalem the Knights of the Hospital of St. John received pilgrims of every faith, fed them on white bread and laid them in clean beds, and called the sick 'our lords'. When the brothers went afield they bore such wands as this, to knit a slashed arm or a cracked rib until a man could go on his way.

wand_of_healing.name: wand of healing
wand_of_healing.lore: The druids of Gaul, as Pliny wrote, went up into the sacred oak in robes of white and cut the mistletoe with a sickle of gold, and they named that plant 'all-heal'. A rod taken from such a tree has in it the slow strength of the oak, and deep wounds close beneath it as bark closes over a scar.

wand_of_greater_healing.name: wand of greater healing
wand_of_greater_healing.lore: Galen of Pergamon learned his surgery among the gladiators, whose wounds he called his windows into the body, and he lost so many fewer than the physician before him that in time he was summoned to heal emperors. The craft he won in the arena is in this rod, and by it one who has been run through rises to his feet again.

wand_of_full_restoration.name: wand of full restoration
wand_of_full_restoration.lore: Asclepius the son of Apollo, whom Chiron the centaur taught, became so great a healer that he called back the dead, until Hades complained that his kingdom was emptying and Zeus slew the physician with a thunderbolt. The makers of this rod halted just short of his offence, and it undoes nearly every harm short of death.

wand_of_fire_spark.name: wand of fire sparks
wand_of_fire_spark.lore: Six Vestal Virgins watched over the hearth of Rome, and if ever the fire died they must kindle it afresh by the rubbing of wood on wood. An apprentice's stick of ash spares such labour, for it spits out orange sparks hot enough to sting a rat or singe a careless sleeve.

wand_of_fire_bolt.name: wand of fire bolt
wand_of_fire_bolt.lore: Against the men of Hannibal the defenders of Saguntum hurled the falarica, a heavy javelin whose iron shank was wrapped in tow and pitch and set alight, and any soldier whose shield received one must cast the shield away. A journeyman with this wand may give the same answer, and he has no need of a javelin.

wand_of_fireball.name: wand of fireball
wand_of_fireball.lore: Kallinikos the builder came a fugitive to Constantinople about the year 672, bringing a liquid fire that was driven through tubes of bronze and burned on upon the very sea. It destroyed two fleets of the Arabs and was so jealously guarded that its making is lost, but its work survives in this wand, as a rolling burst that no water can quench.

wand_of_fire_storm.name: wand of fire storm
wand_of_fire_storm.lore: Three times the prophet Elijah had water poured upon his altar on Mount Carmel, and he prayed but once, and fire fell that consumed bull, wood, stones and dust and licked the trench dry. The masters of flame call down such a column with this rod, and the wall behind their target is left black.

wand_of_cataclysm.name: wand of cataclysm
wand_of_cataclysm.lore: Phaethon begged of his father the chariot of the sun for a single day, and he could not rule the horses, which plunged so near the earth that Libya was burned to desert and the rivers boiled, until Zeus smote the boy from the sky. The tip of this rod glows white before it lets that day's burning loose where the bearer points.

wand_of_static_spark.name: wand of static spark
wand_of_static_spark.lore: Thales of Miletus saw that amber rubbed with fur will draw straws and feathers to itself, and the word that the Greeks had for amber, which was elektron, has outlived them. This stick of a young stormweaver stores a little more than such a bead, and its snapping blue arc lifts the hair and makes small creatures yelp.

wand_of_lightning_bolt.name: wand of lightning bolt
wand_of_lightning_bolt.lore: With a kite of silk flown into a thundercloud in 1752 and sparks drawn from a key upon its string, Benjamin Franklin proved that lightning and the spark of amber are one, and afterward he devised the rod that leads it safely into the earth. But this wand of copper leads it forth instead, in a straight line through whatever stands there.

wand_of_chain_lightning.name: wand of chain lightning
wand_of_chain_lightning.lore: Capaneus climbed against the walls of Thebes crying that Zeus himself could not hinder him, and Zeus struck him from the ladder with one thunderbolt. The bolt of this wand is not spent upon one man, but runs through all who stand in its path and leaves each of them stunned.

wand_of_thunderstorm.name: wand of thunderstorm
wand_of_thunderstorm.lore: An oak sacred to Donar the thunder god grew near Geismar, and about 723 the missionary Boniface laid his axe to it while the people waited for the lightning. None fell, and he built a chapel of the timber, yet master stormweavers still prize thunder-oak for such wands as this, and when one is loosed the air smells of smitten metal.

wand_of_zeus_wrath.name: wand of Zeus's wrath
wand_of_zeus_wrath.lore: Brontes, Steropes and Arges, the three Cyclopes, forged the thunderbolt in thanks to Zeus, who had freed them from Tartarus, and with it he broke the Titans and buried Typhon. The bolt of this wand is white and silent for an eye-blink before it comes with a crack that rattles the teeth of all in the passage.

wand_of_chill.name: wand of chill
wand_of_chill.lore: The north wind Boreas dwelt in a cavern of Thrace, and Athens raised him an altar when his gale had broken four hundred Persian ships off Cape Sepias. One of his lesser breaths is shut in this apprentice's wand, so that the fingers grow numb and whatever it touches moves stiffly for a few steps.

wand_of_cold_bolt.name: wand of cold bolt
wand_of_cold_bolt.lore: The Hrimthursar, the giants of frost, were held by the Norse to be the eldest foes of the gods, a race engendered from the dripping of rime, and journeymen say that their spears were icicles. A single shard of that cold flies from this wand, and where it lands the skin is crusted with frost and the limbs grow slow.

wand_of_frost.name: wand of frost
wand_of_frost.lore: Ere the world was made, as the Norse tell, Niflheim lay northward in mist and ice, and its rime met the sparks of the south in the yawning gap that is called Ginnungagap. This shaft is cold in every season, for the old dark of that place travels with its bolt and leaves a body sluggish.

wand_of_blizzard.name: wand of blizzard
wand_of_blizzard.lore: Before the end shall come Fimbulwinter, so the Eddas foretell, three winters and no summer between, with snow from every quarter and brother turning upon brother for a crust. A little of it escapes at each use of this wand, and a howling of icy needles fills the passage, from which those who live walk away slowly.

wand_of_absolute_zero.name: wand of absolute zero
wand_of_absolute_zero.lore: Dante made the pit of Hell a frozen lake, as though he guessed what Lord Kelvin reckoned out in 1848, that cold has a floor some 273 degrees below freezing where all the motion of matter ceases. The masters of frost have ever reached toward that floor, and for one instant the target of this wand is brought very near it.

wand_of_acid_sting.name: wand of acid sting
wand_of_acid_sting.lore: A great heap of red ants was boiled by the naturalist John Ray in 1671 until he had a sour and biting liquor, the first acid ever won from a living creature, which alchemists call spirit of ants. Their humblest wand squirts a drop much like it, and it raises welts and leaves a lingering sickness.

wand_of_acid_spray.name: wand of acid spray
wand_of_acid_spray.lore: A rock barred the road of Hannibal in the Alps until his engineers, as Livy says, heated it with great fires and drenched it with sour wine, so that it crumbled. This wand needs no fire for that work, for its green spray spreads hissing over scale and plate, and whatever it wets grows sick.

wand_of_acid_blast.name: wand of acid blast
wand_of_acid_blast.lore: Some alchemist of old made long study of the bombardier beetle, which keeps two humours apart in its belly and, when they mingle and boil, shoots the scalding spray from a turret that it can aim over its own back. He fashioned this wand after it, and where the drops fall stone is pitted and flesh fares worse.

wand_of_corrosion.name: wand of corrosion
wand_of_corrosion.lore: Nessus the centaur, as he died, gave Deianira his blood for a love charm, but the venom of the Hydra was in it, and when she had smeared a shirt with it and Heracles put it on, the cloth ate into him and would not be drawn off. This wand bears the same clinging ruin, and the sickness that follows is long.

wand_of_dissolution.name: wand of dissolution
wand_of_dissolution.lore: Paracelsus gave a name to the alkahest, the water that should dissolve all things, and van Helmont sought it for many years, but when Johann Kunckel asked in what jar such a thing was to be kept there was none who could answer him. Neither is the alkahest in this wand, yet armour, hide and bone can scarcely tell the difference.

wand_of_force_dart.name: wand of force dart
wand_of_force_dart.lore: No slingers of the ancient world could equal those of the Balearic Isles, whose mothers, it is told, set a boy's bread upon a post and let him eat only when he had struck it down with a stone. Their craft is copied in this apprentice's wand, which throws a small hard dart of nothing at all that no armour turns.

wand_of_magic_missile.name: wand of magic missile
wand_of_magic_missile.lore: The sons of Ivaldi, who were dwarves, made the spear Gungnir for Odin with this great virtue, that when once it was thrown it could not miss. Mages have copied that virtue and no other into their common wand, whose bolt of force goes round cover and through smoke into the thing at which it was pointed.

wand_of_force_barrage.name: wand of force barrage
wand_of_force_barrage.lore: The archers of England loosed so swiftly at Crecy in 1346 that a chronicler likened their arrows to falling snow, and the Genoese crossbowmen who faced them broke after a single volley. In that fashion this wand answers a charging foe, with bolt upon bolt and no space between in which to lift a shield.

wand_of_force_storm.name: wand of force storm
wand_of_force_storm.lore: Odysseus came home in rags, and when his own bow was set for a trial he strung it as he sat and shot through the sockets of twelve axes in a row, and then turned upon the suitors. So do the master abjurers save this wand for that one enemy who must never rise again.

wand_of_force_cataclysm.name: wand of force cataclysm
wand_of_force_cataclysm.lore: Archimedes said to King Hiero that he could move the earth if he had a place to stand, and for proof he sat upon the shore and with one hand and a train of pulleys drew a laden ship up the sand. At its height the magic of force is wielded likewise, with scarcely any stirring of the hand.

wand_of_rap.name: wand of rap
wand_of_rap.lore: The schoolmasters of Rome ruled with the ferula, a dry stalk of giant fennel, light to hold and bitter to the knuckles, which Martial the poet named the sceptre of teachers. One such stalk was afterward enchanted to strike far beyond its weight, though it is best used upon such creatures as cannot strike back.

wand_of_striking.name: wand of striking
wand_of_striking.lore: When the people cried out for water at Horeb, Moses smote the rock with his staff and the water came. The journeyman's wand has a lesser purpose but no light hand, for its tip flashes and the blow falls as from a hammer of war, though none in the room is holding one.

wand_of_slam.name: wand of slam
wand_of_slam.lore: A beam capped with a ram's head of bronze was swung by the Romans on chains beneath a wheeled shed, and by their custom any town that yielded before the ram had touched its wall was spared. No such mercy is offered by this wand, whose blow cracks shields and dints the breastplates behind them.

wand_of_smite.name: wand of smite
wand_of_smite.lore: Samson stood bound at Lehi when the Philistines came shouting against him, but the Spirit of the Lord came upon him, so that he took up the fresh jawbone of an ass and smote a thousand men. Without any jawbone the wand gives such a blow, as from a righteous arm, and armour buckles inward before it.

wand_of_devastation.name: wand of devastation
wand_of_devastation.lore: Three times Thor swung Mjolnir at the head of a sleeping giant, who woke and asked if a leaf had fallen on him, for by craft the giant had set a mountain between them, and three square valleys remain in it from those blows. This rod strikes as hard, and the stone behind its target keeps the shape of the stroke.

wand_of_drowsing.name: wand of drowsing
wand_of_drowsing.lore: Argus of the hundred eyes was set by Hera to guard the heifer Io, but Hermes sat down by him, piping upon the reeds and telling a long tale, until every eye was closed. The wand of a hedge-witch has that art in less time, and for a short while the eyelids droop, though a blow will wake the sleeper.

wand_of_sleep.name: wand of sleep
wand_of_sleep.lore: Hypnos, the god of sleep, was promised one of the Graces for his bride by Hera, and for that price he perched in a pine on Mount Ida and laid Zeus himself in slumber while the war at Troy went as she wished. This wand is as bold, and its target folds where it stands and lies until it is hurt.

wand_of_deep_slumber.name: wand of deep slumber
wand_of_deep_slumber.lore: For giving the victory to the wrong king the valkyrie Brynhild was pricked by Odin with the sleep-thorn and laid upon a mountain in a ring of fire, and there she slept in her mail until Sigurd rode through the flame and cut it from her. Even great beasts are overcome by such a sleep from this wand.

wand_of_slow.name: wand of slow
wand_of_slow.lore: Atalanta would wed none but the man who should outrun her, and there was none, until Hippomenes let fall a golden apple of Aphrodite each time she passed him, and she stooped for all three and lost. This apprentice's wand is such an apple, and for a little while the target cannot keep its pace.

wand_of_torpor.name: wand of torpor
wand_of_torpor.lore: Ten days out from Troy, Odysseus came among the Lotus-Eaters, and those of his men who tasted the fruit cared no more to row, to bring back word or to go home, so that he dragged them weeping to the ships and bound them beneath the benches. This wand feeds a foe that fruit, and its blows come a beat late.

wand_of_time_halt.name: wand of time halt
wand_of_time_halt.lore: Oisin dwelt in Tir na nOg, the Land of the Young, for what seemed three years, and came home to find that three hundred years had passed in Ireland and all whom he knew were dust. This wand bends time so about one enemy, which still moves, but as honey moves, and the bearer may well be patient.

wand_of_bewilderment.name: wand of bewilderment
wand_of_bewilderment.lore: A traveller astray in a field he knew well was said in the west of England to be pixy-led, and his cure was to turn his coat inside out. Few monsters have coats to turn, and when this wand of some prankster has done the pixies' work the target cannot for a short space tell which way is forward.

wand_of_confusion.name: wand of confusion
wand_of_confusion.lore: Upon the plain of Babel men built their tower toward heaven, until on a morning no company could understand the next, and the bricks were moved no more and the people were scattered over the earth. What befell that plain this wand brings on a single mind, so that the target reels and strikes at whoever is nearest.

wand_of_madness.name: wand of madness
wand_of_madness.lore: Ajax, when the armour of Achilles was given to Odysseus, went out by night to slay the chiefs of the Greeks, but Athena darkened his sight and he slaughtered a flock of sheep, taking them for kings, and woke among the carcasses. This wand unseats a mind as wholly, and it is long before it is restored.

wand_of_hold.name: wand of hold
wand_of_hold.lore: Theseus went down with Pirithous to carry off the queen of the dead, and Hades received them courteously and bade them be seated, whereupon the stone held them fast, and Theseus sat until Heracles came and tore him free. The binder's apprentice offers that seat with this wand, though the target is held for a moment only.

wand_of_paralysis.name: wand of paralysis
wand_of_paralysis.lore: The angels bade Lot's household flee from Sodom and not look behind them, but his wife looked back, and where she stood she became a pillar of salt. The guides beside the Dead Sea still show a column to travellers and call it by her name. As she was stayed, so is any creature that this wand catches, halted in mid-step until the hold breaks.

wand_of_petrifaction.name: wand of petrifaction
wand_of_petrifaction.lore: Niobe, the mother of fourteen children, boasted herself greater than Leto, who had only two, but those two were Apollo and Artemis. Their arrows slew her children, and she wept for them until she hardened into a rock upon Mount Sipylus, from which the water drips yet. The same stillness this wand lays upon living flesh, for as long as its hold endures.

wand_of_terror.name: wand of terror
wand_of_terror.lore: Ares drove to war with his two sons at the yoke of his chariot, Phobos who is Fear and Deimos who is Dread, and in 1877 an astronomer named the two small moons of Mars for them. A whisper of the elder brother lives in this fright-stick of the hedge-witches, and whoever it is turned upon loses all courage and looks about for a door to flee by.

wand_of_fear.name: wand of fear
wand_of_fear.lore: While the dragon Fafnir lay upon his gold he wore the Helm of Awe, and no living thing dared come near him. Sigurd bore it away with the rest of the hoard, and in after times the men of Iceland drew its eight-armed sign between their brows. The wand casts that same dread upon a single enemy, so that it forgets all else and runs.

wand_of_panic_wave.name: wand of panic wave
wand_of_panic_wave.lore: Pan the goat-god was blamed by the Greeks for every sudden terror that had no cause, for his shout from the hills could stampede a herd or an army. He routed the Persians at Marathon, as they told it, and from his name such fear is called panic. When this wand gives that shout, all that are in sight, save the mightiest, flee headlong away.

wand_of_dimming.name: wand of dimming
wand_of_dimming.lore: Lot had angels for his guests in Sodom, and the men of the city crowded about his door, meaning them harm. The angels drew him within and smote the mob with blindness, so that they wearied themselves with groping for the door. A hedge-mage's wand will cloud an enemy's eyes in like fashion, though only for a little while.

wand_of_blindness.name: wand of blindness
wand_of_blindness.lore: Elymas the sorcerer strove in Cyprus to turn the Roman governor from the preaching of Paul, until Paul looked steadily upon him and said that he should be blind for a season. Then a mist fell on the man, and he went about seeking someone to lead him by the hand. The wand passes the same sentence of blindness upon an enemy.

wand_of_dark_curse.name: wand of dark curse
wand_of_dark_curse.lore: For three days, in the ninth of the plagues, there lay upon Egypt a darkness that could be felt, and no man saw his neighbour or rose from his place, though the Israelites had light where they dwelt. This wand wraps a single creature in that darkness, so that the world is wholly lost to it, and for a long while is not given back.

wand_of_rebuke.name: wand of rebuke
wand_of_rebuke.lore: When a priest blesses water he prays that every unclean spirit may flee the place where it is sprinkled, and so precious was that water in the Middle Ages that parishes locked their fonts against thieves. A novice's wand carries the same blessing, and all the walking dead in sight are scalded by its light and turn away.

wand_of_turn_undead.name: wand of turn undead
wand_of_turn_undead.lore: In 1614 the Church gathered her prayers of exorcism into one book, the Roman Ritual, and for three and a half centuries the rite was said with scarcely a change. Its commands of departure are held within this wand of a senior cleric, and the dead things that hear them burn with holy fire and flee as swiftly as they are able.

wand_of_sunburst.name: wand of sunburst
wand_of_sunburst.lore: At the Easter Vigil the church waits in darkness until a new fire is kindled outside the door, and then a deacon bears the flame up the aisle, singing three times that this is the light of Christ. All that moment is gathered in the rod and loosed at once. Before it the lesser dead are unmade where they stand, and the greater are put to flight.

wand_of_small_polymorph.name: wand of small polymorph
wand_of_small_polymorph.lore: The boy Gwion fled from Ceridwen when he had tasted three drops from her cauldron, and he became a hare and she a greyhound, he a fish and she an otter, he a bird and she a hawk, and at last he a grain of wheat and she a hen. A journeyman's wand runs one course of that chase, and no one may choose what shape comes out of it.

wand_of_polymorph.name: wand of polymorph
wand_of_polymorph.lore: Proteus, the Old Man of the Sea, knew all things and would tell none of them unless he were held fast. Menelaus seized him among his seals and held on while he became a lion, a serpent, a leopard, a boar, running water and a tall tree, until he yielded. So does this wand turn one creature into another, but whether for better or worse is left to luck.

wand_of_curse_of_the_menagerie.name: wand of curse of the menagerie
wand_of_curse_of_the_menagerie.lore: Some two hundred and fifty changes of shape are told in the Metamorphoses, which Ovid finished about the year 8. There Lycaon the tyrant was made a wolf, Arachne the weaver a spider, and Actaeon the hunter a stag before his own hounds. The rod writes one creature more into that poem, and none save the mightiest may escape the change.

wand_of_charm.name: wand of charm
wand_of_charm.lore: Francis of Assisi went out alone to meet the wolf that was killing the folk of Gubbio. He called it Brother Wolf and offered a bargain, that the town would feed it if it would do no more harm, and the wolf laid its paw in his hand. The same peace is made by this wand between its bearer and a creature, though only for a while.

wand_of_greater_charm.name: wand of greater charm
wand_of_greater_charm.lore: So sweetly sang Orpheus that trees drew up their roots to come nearer and rivers stayed to listen, and when he went down with his lyre to the underworld, Cerberus lay down, the Furies wept, and Hades consented to give back his wife. One of his songs is held in this wand of a master enchanter, and even hardened creatures will stand still to hear it.

wand_of_dominion.name: wand of dominion
wand_of_dominion.lore: It is an old legend that the archangel Michael brought King Solomon a ring with a seal graven upon it, whereby the king commanded the very demons and set them to hew stone for the Temple. The rod has borrowed that seal's authority, and the creature it is turned upon is more than softened, for it waits upon the bearer as a subject waits upon a king.

wand_of_candle_light.name: wand of candle light
wand_of_candle_light.lore: For many centuries the Church held that the candles of the altar should be of beeswax, for bees were thought pure and the flame burned clean. Apprentices shape this wand like the stub of such a candle from a parish chandler's shop. It casts about you a small warm circle that stays for a while, enough to show a few paces more of the floor and whatever is standing upon them.

wand_of_torch_light.name: wand of torch light
wand_of_torch_light.lore: Demeter lit two pine torches at the fires of Etna when Hades had carried off her daughter Persephone, and for nine days she searched the earth, neither eating nor resting. An explorer's wand burns as one of those torches did, for its tip flares and goes on burning about you, so that more of every chamber is shown to your eyes.

wand_of_sunlight.name: wand of sunlight
wand_of_sunlight.lore: Helios misses nothing as he drives the sun across the sky, and it was he who told Hephaestus of his wife's doings, and he who told Demeter whither her daughter had been taken. A master's wand opens his eye for an instant over a whole floor, so that every passage is seen, and whatever hid there unseen is stripped of its hiding.

wand_of_wonder.name: wand of wonder
wand_of_wonder.lore: Pandora was sent to mankind by Zeus with a great storage jar that she was forbidden to open, and when she opened it every trouble flew out and Hope alone stayed beneath the lid. It was Erasmus who mistook the jar for a box in translating the tale. None can tell what this wand will let out, be it mending, fire, sleep or a sudden change of place.

wand_of_greater_wonder.name: wand of greater wonder
wand_of_greater_wonder.lore: While Boethius lay in prison awaiting his death, about the year 524, he beheld in thought the Lady Fortune at her wheel, who laughs alike at the kings who rise on one side and at those who fall on the other. A master's wand of wonder turns the same wheel as the lesser kind with a stronger hand, and its good turns are better, though nothing else is promised.

wand_of_chaos.name: wand of chaos
wand_of_chaos.lore: Eris, the goddess of strife, alone was not bidden to the wedding of Peleus and Thetis, so she rolled a golden apple among the goddesses, marked 'for the fairest', and of it came ten years of war at Troy. This rod is such an apple, and every time it is used the bearer is as much amazed at what follows as the enemy.

wand_of_digging.name: wand of digging
wand_of_digging.lore: King John laid siege to Rochester Castle in 1215 and set miners to dig beneath a corner of the keep. Then he sent for forty of the fattest pigs in the county and burned their lard in the tunnel, until the props gave way and the tower fell. The wand has no need of miners or of pigs, and at its word the walls and doors around its bearer burst open.

wand_of_cancellation.name: wand of cancellation
wand_of_cancellation.lore: From morning until noon four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal cried upon their god on Carmel, leaping and cutting themselves, while Elijah mocked them that he must be asleep, and no answer came. That same silence this wand brings upon an enemy's magic, and every ward and blessing that the creature wore goes out at once.

wand_of_drain_magic.name: wand of drain magic
wand_of_drain_magic.lore: A slave girl at Philippi had a spirit of divination and earned much gold for her owners by telling fortunes. For days she followed Paul, until he turned and bade the spirit depart, and when it left her the gain of her owners departed with it. As suddenly as that, this wand empties a creature of all the power it has borrowed.

wand_of_dispel_magic.name: wand of dispel magic
wand_of_dispel_magic.lore: The magicians of Pharaoh matched the first signs of Moses and Aaron, for they too made serpents, turned water to blood and called up frogs. But at the third plague, which was of gnats, their arts failed them, and they told their master that this was the finger of God. So the contest ends when this wand is raised, and every enchantment upon your enemy ceases at once.

wand_of_teleport_monster.name: wand of teleport monster
wand_of_teleport_monster.lore: Hephaestus once took his mother's part in a quarrel, and Zeus caught him by the foot and flung him from Olympus, so that he fell the whole day and came to earth at sunset upon the isle of Lemnos. As freely does a conjurer's wand hurl a creature to some far corner of the floor, though afterward it may come walking back.

wand_of_poison_monster.name: wand of poison monster
wand_of_poison_monster.lore: Heracles dipped his arrows in the gall of the Hydra, and thereafter their least scratch was death. One of them grazed the wise centaur Chiron, who was immortal and so could not die of it, and in his torment he begged to give his immortality away. The alchemist's wand works more slowly than those arrows, but its poison is as patient as theirs.

wand_of_disease_monster.name: wand of disease monster
wand_of_disease_monster.lore: Apollo came down from Olympus like nightfall when Agamemnon had insulted his priest, as the Iliad tells at its beginning, and for nine days he shot plague into the camp of the Greeks, slaying first the mules and dogs and afterward the men. This wand looses one arrow from that quiver, and the sickness hurts at once and goes on hurting.

wand_of_curse_monster.name: wand of curse monster
wand_of_curse_monster.lore: At the hot spring of Bath, Romans who had been wronged would scratch their complaints on little sheets of lead, roll them up and cast them to the goddess Sulis. About a hundred and thirty have been drawn out again, and most pray her to ruin some thief who stole a cloak. The hexer's wand bears such a prayer, and brings ill luck and heavy feet upon an enemy.

wand_of_weaken_monster.name: wand of weaken monster
wand_of_weaken_monster.lore: In the hall of Utgard-Loki Thor was challenged to wrestle the king's old nurse, a crone named Elli, and the harder he gripped the firmer she stood, until she forced him down on one knee. For Elli was Old Age, who overthrows all the living at last, and this wand lends a few of her years to an enemy, so that its strength fails.

wand_of_secret_door_detection.name: wand of secret door detection
wand_of_secret_door_detection.lore: Georgius Agricola, in the great book of mining that was printed in 1556, showed men walking the hills with forked hazel twigs that dipped above hidden veins of ore, though he himself doubted the craft. In these depths it holds true, and a dungeoneer's wand will twitch toward the false wall until the door behind it is plain to see.

wand_of_opening.name: wand of opening
wand_of_opening.lore: Peter lay chained between two soldiers in Herod's prison, with sentries at the door, when an angel woke him in the night, and the chains fell from his wrists and the iron gate of the city opened to them of itself. No angel comes with a thief-mage's wand, yet at its bidding every door in sight swings wide and every locked chest clicks open.

wand_of_probing.name: wand of probing
wand_of_probing.lore: Andreas Vesalius opened the bodies of the dead with his own hands, and in 1543 he published seven books upon the fabric of the human body, with drawings of what he had found, which overturned errors that had stood since the days of Galen. A scholar's wand makes the same honest examination and has no need of the knife. It tells how much life is left in a creature and of what it is made, and thereafter its kind is known to you as surely as if you had studied its corpse.

wand_of_death_ray.name: wand of death ray
wand_of_death_ray.lore: Balor, the king of the Fomorians, had one eye that slew all it looked upon. In battle four men must lift its lid by a polished handle, and whole companies fell before it, until his grandson Lugh put a sling stone through it. This rod opens that eye for a single glance, and none but the mightiest will live through it, and those sorely hurt.

wand_of_disintegrate.name: wand of disintegrate
wand_of_disintegrate.lore: Semele desired of Zeus that he would come to her in his true form, as he came to Hera, and he had sworn by the Styx to grant her wish. No mortal might bear that sight, and she was burned to ash where she stood. A sliver of the same glory is in the beam of this rod, and whatever it touches will usually cease to be.

wand_of_life_drain.name: wand of life drain
wand_of_life_drain.lore: Odysseus dug a trench at the edge of the world and filled it with the blood of a ram and a black ewe, and the shades of the dead came crowding to drink, for blood alone gave them strength to speak. A necromancer's wand strikes the same bargain, drawing the life out of its victim and giving it over to the bearer.

wand_of_soul_drain.name: wand of soul drain
wand_of_soul_drain.lore: The striges, of which Ovid has told, were birds with hooked beaks and grey feathers that flew by night to feed at the cradles of unguarded infants, and the nurses of Rome hung whitethorn in their windows against them. Their hunger is in this wand of a master necromancer, and it draws a great draught of an enemy's life across the room to you.

caduceus_wand.name: Caduceus of Hermes
caduceus_wand.unidentified_name: a golden rod entwined with two serpents
caduceus_wand.lore: Hermes, the herald of the gods, bore the caduceus, a winged rod with two serpents twined about it, and beneath that sign messengers passed unharmed. The true emblem of medicine is the staff of Asclepius with its single snake, but in 1902 the United States Army Medical Corps took up the caduceus in error, and the confusion has endured. In this matter the dungeon holds with the Army, and so the rod heals, and heals well.

lantern_of_diogenes.name: Lantern of Diogenes
lantern_of_diogenes.lore: Diogenes of Sinope dwelt in a storage jar in the marketplace of Athens and owned a cloak, a staff and a bag, and when Alexander the Great offered him any favour, he asked only that the king should stand out of his sunlight. He would walk the streets at noon with a lantern burning, and said that he sought an honest man. The lantern burns yet, and while it lights a whole chamber it is searching still for any who may be hidden there.

iron_mortar_wand.name: Baba Yaga's Iron Mortar
iron_mortar_wand.lore: Baba Yaga grinds the bones of heroes in this mortar before she eats them. Whoever wields it as a wand sets loose the chaos of her magic, and it never works twice in the same fashion.

aarons_rod.name: Aaron's Rod
aarons_rod.lore: Aaron, the brother of Moses, cast this rod down before Pharaoh's court, and it became a serpent and swallowed the serpents of the magicians. Later, when the tribes disputed, it budded almonds in a night to settle the matter, as is written in Exodus 7 and Numbers 17. Whatever foe rises against its bearer, the rod takes the legs from under it, so that it cannot stir.

circes_wand.name: Circe's Wand
circes_wand.lore: Upon the isle of Aeaea dwelt Circe, the daughter of the Sun, in a house of polished stone with tame wolves and lions at the door. She gave drugged wine to the crew of Odysseus, touched them with her wand and drove them into her sties as swine that had the minds of men, but against Odysseus himself her magic failed, for Hermes had given him the herb moly. In other hands the wand has grown careless, and though it will still change a creature, no one may choose what that creature shall become.

indras_vajra.name: Indra's Vajra
indras_vajra.lore: When the serpent Vritra lay coiled upon the mountains and hoarded all the waters, Tvastr the craftsman-god fashioned for Indra the thunderbolt that is called the vajra. With it, as the Rigveda sings, Indra split the serpent open, and the seven rivers ran down to the sea. In later days it was told that the bolt was made from the bones of the sage Dadhichi, who yielded up his body that the gods might have their weapon, and when it is loosed it runs through all who stand in a line.

ruby_rod.name: Ruby Rod of Asmodeus
ruby_rod.lore: Seven husbands of Sarah were slain by the demon Asmodeus, each upon his wedding night, as the Book of Tobit tells. Then the angel Raphael taught young Tobias to drive him out with the smoke of a fish's heart and liver, and himself pursued the demon to Upper Egypt and bound him there. Later ages made Asmodeus a king of Hell and gave this sceptre into his hand, and the fire within its ruby has never cooled, so that the rod can spend it freely.
ruby_rod.design_notes: Asmodeus L92 boss drop. Wired via monster.treasure.unique_drop_id.

wand_of_unstringing.name: wand of unstringing
wand_of_unstringing.lore: Young Joukahainen drove his sledge against old Vainamoinen's upon the road and challenged him to a match of singing. Then the old singer sang the boy's bow into a rainbow over the lake, his arrows into hawks, his sledge into reeds and the boy himself into the swamp up to the chin. The song abides in birch wood that was cut where they met, and if that wood is pointed at a creature, its long weapons will answer no more to its hand.

krotala_of_athena.name: Krotala of Athena
krotala_of_athena.lore: Heracles could neither walk upon the marsh of Lake Stymphalia nor shoot into its thickets, where the man-eating birds lay hid, so Athena gave him these bronze clappers of Hephaestus's making. At their dreadful clatter the whole flock burst upward out of the reeds, and in each charge there is one such great clash of bronze.
krotala_of_athena.zap_line: You clash the bronze krotala, and the din is dreadful: every bird in sight bursts up and flies.
krotala_of_athena.none_line: You clash the bronze, and the din rolls round the walls. No bird is in sight to fly from it.
